title: Spectroscopic signatures of persistent exciton condensation in a bulk magnetic topological insulator
authors: Paulina Majchrzak, Chakradhar Sahoo, Manuel Tuniz, Wibke Bronsch, Denny Puntel, Federico Cilento, Xing-Chen Pan, Jakob Kjærulff Svaneborg, Yong P. Chen, Søren Ulstrup
abstract: Exciton condensates are long-sought correlated quantum states arising from macroscopic coherence of bound electron-hole pairs. Although equilibrium and transient excitonic states have been reported in several material platforms, direct evidence for a light-induced exciton condensate state has been challenging to achieve as an intrinsic property of a bulk quantum material. Here, we use time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate long-lived photoexcited carriers in the intrinsic magnetic topological insulator MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ with the chemical potential tuned to the topological surface state by Sb substitution. Following optical excitation, we observe the delayed emergence of a transient state whose formation coincides with depopulation of the bulk conduction band and whose lifetime extends to the microsecond timescale. The quasiparticle dispersion exhibits a pronounced flattening and develops a Mexican-hat-like profile. These spectral signatures are consistent with the formation of a metastable excitonic condensate state. Our results establish magnetic topological insulators as a promising platform for investigating long-lived photoinduced many-body states and their interplay with topology and magnetism.
summary: This experimental study uses trARPES on a magnetic topological insulator to investigate light-induced exciton condensation. By observing a transient state with a characteristic Mexican-hat dispersion and long lifetime, the authors provide strong evidence for a metastable, BCS-like excitonic condensate. This work establishes magnetic topological insulators as a promising platform for studying correlated many-body physics.
main_problem: The study aims to find direct evidence for a light-induced exciton condensate (EC) state within the bulk of a quantum material.
main_result: The authors observed spectral signatures, including a Mexican-hat-like quasiparticle dispersion and a microsecond lifetime, consistent with the formation of a metastable BCS-type excitonic condensate.
method: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (trARPES) was employed to probe the evolution of photoexcited carriers over time delays.
model_or_system: The physical system is an intrinsic magnetic topological insulator, specifically MnBi2Te4 doped with Sb to tune the chemical potential into the topological surface state. The analysis focuses on the many-body physics of photoexcited electron-hole pairs.
key_observables: Quasiparticle dispersion shape (Mexican-hat profile), transient state lifetime (microsecond scale), Exciton Binding Energy (EB), and BCS gap ($\Delta$).
important_parameters: Temperature (110 K vs 300 K), doping concentration (Sb substitution), and time delay ($\Delta t$).
main_assumptions: The observed spectral signatures are interpreted as evidence for a metastable excitonic condensate state, and the analysis relies on fitting procedures like Lorentzian functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of Energy-Distribution Curves (EDCs) showing peak flattening and the development of the Mexican-hat shape over time, alongside comparisons of spectra taken through and away from the proposed EC state.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the experimental setup and tuning the material into the topological surface state, then presenting time-resolved measurements showing the delayed emergence of a transient state, and finally analyzing the spectral features (dispersion, gap opening) to confirm the BCS-like nature of the condensate.
why_interesting: The work bridges concepts from topological physics (TSS) with strongly correlated many-body physics (excitonic condensation), providing an experimental platform to study non-equilibrium correlated states in novel materials.
